topItems.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
topItems.excerpt: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping...

brief.whatHappened: Simon Willison published "Ladybird's first alpha release". Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly.
brief.whyItMatters: The platform is the one dependency every web project shares. A feature reaching all browsers removes a library, and a regression explains a bug you did not write.

keyConcepts.explanation: A compact binary format browsers run at near-native speed, used to bring code written in Rust, C++ or Go to the web.
A label from the web standards community that tells you a feature works in all major browsers, and since when.
